A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose the idea of using a unified methodology, based on PAPI, to monitor both the Hw and Sw elements of heterogeneous systems and we validate this idea by means of a case study.

we propose a PAPI compliant monitoring infrastructure for Hw/Sw heterogeneous architectures, based on the PAPIFY library, which can be used in combination with the MDC automatic design flow to instrument run time reconfigurables systems.

we propose to use the Performance Application Programming interface (PAPI) for monitoring the performance of heterogeneous systems, where the processing elements are connected to custom reconfigurable hardware accelerators.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the monitoring of the internal system status can be achieved using a single unified interface, that is transparent to the Sw developers, and that is independent on the underlying Hw architecture.

PAPIFY is a lightweight and effective monitoring infrastructure for embedded heterogeneous systems, and it offers a unified methodology to monitor both the standard PMCs in the CPU and the custom monitors integrated in the accelerators.
